Ava (CEO): thanks for joining the follow-up. quick Q&A about our mission and how we position vs model vendors and infra players. i'll be here for 20. keep Qs tight.
Kai (Head of GTM): real ask from sales: what is the single best sentence to win an exec meeting vs a model vendor?
Maya (Head of Strategy): try: 'We take the operational risk out of running LLMs in production — predictable latency, measurable unit economics, and enterprise-grade controls across hosted, dedicated, and private.'
Noah (Eng): we often get asked if we care more about latency or cost. how do we advise engineers?
Priya (Product): default to latency SLOs + predictable p99s for UX-critical flows, then use Optimize to reduce cost without regressing quality.
Kai (Head of GTM): competitor pushback: "we can run models ourselves cheaper." short rebuttal?
Ava (CEO): short: 'Maybe, but building and operating the full stack to meet SLAs and rollout safety is expensive — we provide that as a product so your team ships features, not infra.'
Maya (Head of Strategy): add: emphasize token-level cost attribution and rollout primitives. those are operational levers customers can't easily replicate.
Noah (Eng): technical competitor q: do we publicly name that we do prefix caching and continuous batching? would that help sales?
Priya (Product): be specific where it helps: in docs and benchmark snippets we call out caching, batching, and quantization impacts. on sales calls, tailor the depth to the buyer.
Kai (Head of GTM): market focus question: should we shift more effort into regulated verticals (finserv/health) now or go broad?
Maya (Head of Strategy): go vertical selectively — pick 2 regulated pilots where Private + KMS/HSM deliver clear wins. wins there also create enterprise motion.
Ava (CEO): agreed. prioritize a few high-impact pilots, use those case studies to tune the Private product.
Noah (Eng): roadmap ask: any change to public benchmark cadence? customers want repeatable numbers.
Priya (Product): we'll publish monthly perf notes for curated models and document perf tradeoffs by deployment mode.
Kai (Head of GTM): one more: what are the three sales objections we should always preempt?
Maya (Head of Strategy): 1) "We already have infra" -> show ops savings. 2) "We own models" -> show model support & private deploy. 3) "Costs too high" -> show Dedicated economics + Optimize wins.

Ava (CEO): great thread. i'll post the short lines into the sales and marketing channels and share a competitive brief with the GTM team. book time with Maya/Priya for deeper dives. thanks! :clap:
